# openssh — 2016 high-value CVEs (CVSS>=7, CISA KEV, Exploit-DB, or SSVC exploitation active/poc)

Full records for all 16 openssh CVEs of 2016 are in `data/cve/vendors/openssh/2016.jsonl`.

### CVE-2016-0778
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2016-01-14 | Updated: 2026-05-29 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: n/a; CWE-119 CWE-119 Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The (1) roaming_read and (2) roaming_write functions in roaming_common.c in the client in OpenSSH 5.x, 6.x, and 7.x before 7.1p2, when certain proxy and forward options are enabled, do not properly maintain connection file descriptors, which allows remote servers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact by requesting many forwardings.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2016-1908
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2017-04-11 | Updated: 2026-05-29 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-287 CWE-287 Improper Authentication
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

The client in OpenSSH before 7.2 mishandles failed cookie generation for untrusted X11 forwarding and relies on the local X11 server for access-control decisions, which allows remote X11 clients to trigger a fallback and obtain trusted X11 forwarding privileges by leveraging configuration issues on this X11 server, as demonstrated by lack of the SECURITY extension on this X11 server.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2016-3115
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2016-03-22 | Updated: 2026-05-29 | Max CVSS: 6.4

- Exploit-DB 39569: OpenSSH 7.2p1 - (Authenticated) xauth Command Injection (remote/multiple, 2016-03-16, verified=0)

### CVE-2016-6210
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2017-02-13 | Updated: 2026-05-29 | Max CVSS: 5.9
- CWE: n/a; CWE-200 CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 5.9 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- Exploit-DB 40136: OpenSSH 7.2p2 - Username Enumeration (remote/linux, 2016-07-20, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 40113: OpenSSHd 7.2p2 - Username Enumeration (remote/linux, 2016-07-18, verified=0)

sshd in OpenSSH before 7.3, when SHA256 or SHA512 are used for user password hashing, uses BLOWFISH hashing on a static password when the username does not exist, which allows remote attackers to enumerate users by leveraging the timing difference between responses when a large password is provided.

### CVE-2016-10012
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2017-01-05 | Updated: 2026-05-29 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-119 CWE-119 Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The shared memory manager (associated with pre-authentication compression) in sshd in OpenSSH before 7.4 does not ensure that a bounds check is enforced by all compilers, which might allows local users to gain privileges by leveraging access to a sandboxed privilege-separation process, related to the m_zback and m_zlib data structures.
